## Historical audit: S0086, visible chunk 1 of 3

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/generic_same_structured_evidence/C1/selection/commons_133800864/trajectory.jsonl`. Line references below are to this file. Neither the reference nor rendered images are visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The task was to reconstruct a single indoor photograph with editable SceneAct/Blender geometry, matching viewpoint, framing, objects and materials. The student received an image path; the kitchen interpretation and image-space anchors are the student’s inferences, not independently verified facts. |
| Student response, line 3; execution, line 4 | The first program constructed multiple separate scene assets: walls and counter, cabinet, window and blinds, roll, ring, sink, canister, blender, jug and pitcher. It specified procedural stone and cloth textures, reflective hardware, camera and lights. Parts were grouped in assets; the towel was separately linked, so visual contact and physical connection are not established by grouping. The cup and pitcher lid were tilted; actual pose matching is unverified. |
| Execution result, line 5; selection, line 6 | Step 1 reported `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file, and was selected. The log reports 16 render samples despite the program requesting 48. This is execution evidence, not visual or geometric validation. |
| Student request, line 7; student response, line 9 | The runner supplied the result and render for comparison. The student diagnosed cropped pitcher and roll, low upper fittings and pale lighting. These are student observations, not independently checked image findings. The revision widened the lens from 67 to 44, changed aim, raised fittings, broadened the towel, added a jug handle, and darkened surfaces and lighting. It also parented the towel and label to named groups; that does not prove correct contact. |
| Execution, line 10; result, line 11; selection, line 12 | Step 2 was executed, reported `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file, and was selected. The visible trace ends there; no later review or final submission is visible. |

**Teacher and exploration.** No teacher-specific input, detection, diagnosis or proposed update is visible in this chunk, and no teacher adoption can be established. The comparison instruction came from the runner/user message. The student’s own render review drove the visible revision. Both recorded CLI sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2 and 8); this does not rule out internal reasoning, but provides no evidence of additional autonomous tool exploration.

**Outcome and lessons.** Two builds had formal execution success; overall reconstruction correctness and final outcome remain **unknown**, not established success or failure. A transferable distinction is that a successful render validates execution, not framing, materials or part contact. The particular lens, fitting-height and lighting changes are task-specific attempted corrections; whether they improved the match remains an unresolved hypothesis. Chunks 2–3 and image contents were not inspected or inferred.
